content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To restrain a dog, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Retrieve the heavy-duty nylon leash from the closet (30 seconds)
Step 2. Calm the dog with a soft voice and gentle petting (5 minutes)
Step 3. Check the tension of the harness straps (1 minute)
Step 4. Locate the metal D-ring on the collar (10 seconds)
Step 5. Clear a space in the hallway for the procedure (2 minutes)
Step 6. Double-check the security of the leash clip (20 seconds)
Step 7. Position yourself to the left of the dog (15 seconds)
Step 8. Attach the primary leash to the collar (10 seconds)
Step 9. Apply a secondary safety tether (45 seconds)
Step 10. Open a bag of training treats (15 seconds)
Step 11. Command the dog to sit (10 seconds)
Step 12. Check the buckle for any hair or debris (30 seconds)
Step 13. Ensure the collar is not too tight (20 seconds)
Step 14. Place your hand firmly on the dog's shoulder (5 seconds)
Step 15. Slide the harness over the dog's head (30 seconds)
Step 16. Confirm the dog is comfortable and breathing normally (1 minute)
Step 17. Adjust the chest strap for a snug fit (1 minute)
Step 18. Buckle the underbelly strap of the harness (20 seconds)
Step 19. Hold the dog's favorite toy to keep their attention (2 minutes)
Step 20. Wash your hands to remove any scent of other animals (3 minutes)
Step 21. Tighten the grip on the short-handle lead (5 seconds)
Step 22. Inspect the integrity of the stitching on the gear (4 minutes)
Step 23. Loop the handle of the leash around your wrist (10 seconds)
Step 24. Put on non-slip gloves (1 minute)
Step 25. Offer a small treat to reinforce staying still (10 seconds)
Step 26. Guide the dog into a standing position (20 seconds)
Step 27. Ensure the leash is not tangled around legs (15 seconds)
Step 28. Verify that all clips are locked (10 seconds)
Step 29. Test the range of motion for the dog (1 minute)
Step 30. Check the floor for any slipping hazards (1 minute)
Step 31. Re-evaluate the dog's stress levels (2 minutes)
Step 32. Adjust the length of the lead (30 seconds)
Step 33. Inspect the padding on the harness (2 minutes)
Step 34. Check the surroundings for distractions like cats or squirrels (3 minutes)
Step 35. Prepare a backup slip-lead (1 minute)
Step 36. Call for a helper to stand by (5 minutes)
Step 37. Identify the dog's "flight" triggers (10 minutes)
Step 38. Check the weather for extreme heat or cold (2 minutes)
Step 39. Shorten the leash to a "heel" position (15 seconds)
Step 40. Firmly plant your feet on the ground (5 seconds)
Step 41. Secure the leash to the harness D-ring (10 seconds)
Step 42. Look for the manufacturer's weight limit on the gear (1 minute)
Step 43. Ensure the dog's identification tags are visible (30 seconds)
Step 44. Command the dog to "wait" (10 seconds)
Step 45. Gather all necessary restraint equipment (4 minutes)
Step 46. Ensure the room is quiet and the door is closed (2 minutes)
Step 47. Check your own posture for stability (30 seconds)
Step 48. Scan the immediate area for sharp objects (2 minutes)
Step 49. Inspect the leash for any fraying or tears (2 minutes)
Step 50. Hand a treat to the dog for cooperation (5 seconds)
Step 51. Maintain a firm but gentle hold on the harness handle (1 minute)
Step 52. Check the dog's paws for sensitivity (3 minutes)
Step 53. Set a timer for the duration of the restraint (30 seconds)
Step 54. Signal to the dog that the session is starting (5 seconds)
Step 55. Pull the leash taut to remove slack (5 seconds)
Step 56. Final check of the buckle's "click" sound (5 seconds)
Step 57. Check the dog's ear position for signs of anxiety (1 minute)
Step 58. Lubricate the metal hinges of the clips (5 minutes)
Step 59. Tighten the collar by one notch if necessary (20 seconds)
Step 60. Lay out the secondary leash on the floor (30 seconds)
Step 61. Read the instructions for the specific harness model (10 minutes)
Step 62. Ensure the dog is facing away from the exit (30 seconds)
Step 63. Wrap the leash once around your palm for extra grip (10 seconds)
Step 64. Perform a "tug test" on all connections (15 seconds)
Step 65. Offer words of encouragement (1 minute)
Step 66. Observe the dog's tail carriage (1 minute)
Step 67. Anchor your weight slightly backward (10 seconds)
Step 68. Calmly approach the dog from the side (2 minutes)
Step 69. Lower your center of gravity (10 seconds)
Step 70. Remove any loose jewelry or clothing (1 minute)
